sentences.text: 1  NC: 2024:KHC-K:8321  MFA No. 201695 of 2018  THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT, PRAYING TO, CALL FOR RECORDS AND SET ASIDE THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD PASSED BY THE COURT OF THE III ADDITIONAL DISTRICT JUDGE AND MACT NO.IV, VIJAYAPUR, AT VIJAYAPUR IN MVC NO.314/2014 DATED 13.08.2018 MODIFYING THE IMPUGNED ORDER AND BE PLEASED TO ALLOW THE CLAIM PETITION BY GRANTING THE RELIEF AS PRAYED FOR BY THE APPELLANT.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM
ORAL JUDGMENT
(PER: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM)

This appeal is by the claimant assailing the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.314/2014 fastening negligence to an extent of 50% on the driver of the offending vehicle and also on quantum.
2. The appellant herein filed a claim petition for having sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident dated 16.11.2013.
The appellant was travelling in the offending car bearing number KA-28/N-2626 towards NC: 2024:KHC-K:8321 Bijapur.
The appellant alleged that the driver of the offending car was driving the car in a rash and negligent manner and therefore, collided with the mini lorry bearing number MH-13/R-4844.

3. The Tribunal contrary to the charge sheet filed against the driver of the offending car, however,
taking note of the evidence led in by the claimants, who were the inmates of the car has come to conclusion that the driver of the offending mini lorry was also equally negligent as there was a collision in the middle of the road and therefore claim petition is allowed by directing the insurance company to pay 50% of the compensation by fixing negligence at 50:50.
This finding is under challenge.
Finding on Liability:
4. In the present case on hand, the driver of the offending car is charge sheeted.

The finding of the Tribunal that the insurance company is liable to pay only 50% of the compensation determined by the Tribunal is clearly NC: 2024:KHC-K:8321 perverse and contrary to law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Khenyei Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. & Ors.1.

entities.text: Khenyei Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. & Ors.1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Apex Court has clearly held that in the case of composite negligence, the victim/claimant is entitled to sue any one of the joint tort feasors for recovery of the entire amount of compensation.
The extent of liability has to be independently decided between joint tort feasors.

Even if one of the joint tort feasors is impleaded by the claimant, the insurance company which is impleaded, cannot have a defence that other joint Sourabh vs B.Bhujanga Shetty And Anr on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79415842/

entities.text: Sourabh vs B.Bhujanga Shetty And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2 tort feasors is also equally liable and is a necessary party.
The Apex Court held that intrinsic liability of joint tort feasors is to be worked out independently.

5. In the light of the law laid down by the Apex Court, more particularly when the driver of the offending car is charge sheeted, the finding that insurance company is liable to pay only 50% of the compensation determined 2015 (9) SCC 273 NC: 2024:KHC-K:8321 is perverse.
The second respondent/insurance company is liable to indemnify and pay the entire compensation.
The question of composite negligence has to be worked out by second respondent/company independently.
Finding on Quantum:

6. In absence of income proof, the Tribunal has assessed the income of the appellant at Rs.6,000/-
per month.
This appears to be on the lower side.
In absence of income proof, this Court is inclined to rely on the income chart issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
If income is assessed at Rs.7,000/- and disability is assessed at 10%, the compensation payable under the head of loss of future earning works out to Rs.1,42,800/- (Rs.7,000/- x 12 x 17 x 10%).
The compensation determined under other heads are fair and just and would not warrant any interference.
The compensation re-determined by this Court works out to Rs.3,35,800/-.

In the light of findings recorded supra, this Court passes the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.
ii. The claimant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.1,42,800/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

iii. Respondent No.2/insurance company is liable to pay the entire compensation determined by the Tribunal and by this Court with 6%
interest from the date of petition till realization.
iv. The deposit and release of the enhanced amount shall be in terms of the judgment rendered by the Tribunal.
